title: Measles Cases in the U.S. Reach New Highs as Vaccination Rates Fall
subtitle: Health experts warn that the country may soon lose its status as a place where the disease is no longer a constant threat.

summary.en: The United States has recorded more than 2,300 measles cases so far in 2026. This number is already higher than the total for all of 2025. Experts say that lower vaccination rates are the main reason for this dangerous growth. Measles is an extremely contagious disease that can cause serious health problems. Doctors are now worried that the virus is spreading within communities across the country.
summary.zh: 美國 2026 年至今已記錄超過 2,300 例麻疹病例，此數字已高於 2025 年全年的總和。專家表示，疫苗接種率下降是導致此危險增長的主要原因。麻疹是一種傳染力極強的疾病，可能引發嚴重的健康問題。醫師們目前擔憂病毒正在全美各地的社區內傳播。

paragraphs.en: The United States is currently facing a significant health challenge as measles cases continue to rise. According to the CDC, there have been more than 2,300 confirmed cases of the disease so far this year. This figure is higher than the total number of cases reported for the entire year of 2025. Data from the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health shows that by the middle of July 2026, the number of cases had already reached 2,321. This marks a 35-year high for the country, a concerning milestone that health officials say was entirely preventable.
paragraphs.zh: 美國目前正面臨一項重大的健康挑戰，麻疹病例持續攀升。根據美國疾病管制與預防中心（CDC）的數據，今年至今已確診超過 2,300 例。此數字已超越 2025 年全年的通報總數。約翰霍普金斯大學彭博公共衛生學院（Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health）的資料顯示，截至 2026 年 7 月中旬，病例數已達 2,321 例。這創下了該國 35 年來的新高，衛生官員表示，這是一個令人擔憂的里程碑，且本來是可以完全預防的。

paragraphs.en: Measles was officially eliminated from the United States in the year 2000. In public health terms, elimination means that the virus is no longer constantly spreading within the country. While there were occasional cases after 2000, these were usually brought in by people traveling from other parts of the world. However, Dr. Jennifer Nuzzo, an epidemiologist at the Brown University School of Public Health, notes that the current situation is very different. She explains that the virus is now spreading from person to person within American communities. Because of this, experts expect the U.S. will soon lose its official elimination status.
paragraphs.zh: 麻疹在 2000 年時已正式在美國絕跡。在公共衛生領域中，絕跡意味著該病毒不再於國內持續傳播。雖然 2000 年後偶有零星病例，但通常是由從世界其他地區旅行入境的人員所帶入。然而，布朗大學公共衛生學院（Brown University School of Public Health）的流行病學家珍妮佛·努佐（Jennifer Nuzzo）博士指出，目前的情況大不相同。她解釋說，病毒現在正在美國社區內人傳人。正因如此，專家預計美國很快就會失去其官方認定的絕跡狀態。

paragraphs.en: Many experts believe that a decline in vaccination rates is the primary cause of this resurgence. Dr. Nuzzo points to a growing amount of negative language and misinformation on social media and in political discussions, which suggests that vaccines are not safe or effective. These claims are false, but they have influenced many parents to delay or avoid vaccinating their children. As a result, there are now growing pockets of people who are susceptible, meaning they have no protection against the virus. When enough people in a community are not vaccinated, the virus can easily find new people to infect.
paragraphs.zh: 許多專家認為，疫苗接種率下降是導致疫情復燃的主因。努佐博士指出，社群媒體與政治討論中充斥著越來越多負面言論與錯誤資訊，暗示疫苗不安全或無效。這些說法均屬虛假，卻已影響許多家長延遲或避免讓孩子接種疫苗。結果導致現在出現越來越多缺乏免疫力的人群，意即他們對病毒毫無防護。當社區內有足夠多的人未接種疫苗，病毒便能輕易找到新的感染對象。

paragraphs.en: Measles is known as the most contagious virus on Earth. It spreads through tiny droplets in the air when an infected person breathes, talks, or coughs. Paul Offit, director of the Vaccine Education Center at the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia, warns that the virus can stay in the air for up to two hours after an infected person has left a room. A major danger is that people can spread the virus to others about four days before they even realize they are sick and before any spots or rashes appear on their skin. Because it spreads so easily, even small gaps in vaccination coverage can lead to large outbreaks.
paragraphs.zh: 麻疹被公認為地球上傳染力最強的病毒。當感染者呼吸、說話或咳嗽時，病毒會透過空氣中的微小飛沫傳播。費城兒童醫院（Children's Hospital of Philadelphia）疫苗教育中心主任保羅·奧菲特（Paul Offit）警告，即便感染者離開房間後，病毒仍可在空氣中停留長達兩小時。一大危險在於，人們在意識到自己生病，以及皮膚出現任何斑點或紅疹的前四天，就已經能將病毒傳染給他人。由於傳播極為容易，即便疫苗接種覆蓋率出現微小缺口，也可能導致大規模爆發。

paragraphs.en: For many people, the risks of measles are often underestimated. About one in five people who catch the disease in the U.S. require hospital care. Complications can be severe, including pneumonia, which is a serious lung infection, or encephalitis, a type of brain inflammation that can lead to permanent brain damage. In the worst cases, the disease is fatal. Dr. Offit noted that two previously healthy children died from measles-related pneumonia this past year, describing the experience as a terrible way to suffer. Even for those who recover, the virus can weaken the immune system for years, making it harder for the body to fight off other illnesses. There is also a rare but deadly brain disease that can appear up to a decade after the initial infection.
paragraphs.zh: 對許多人而言，麻疹的風險常被低估。在美國，約每五名感染者中就有一人需要住院治療。併發症可能相當嚴重，包括肺炎（一種嚴重的肺部感染），或是腦炎（一種可能導致永久性腦損傷的腦部發炎）。在最糟的情況下，該疾病會致命。奧菲特博士提到，過去一年有兩名先前健康的兒童死於麻疹引發的肺炎，他形容這種經歷是極其痛苦的折磨。即使是康復者，病毒也可能在數年內削弱免疫系統，使身體更難抵禦其他疾病。此外，還有一種罕見但致命的腦部疾病，可能在初次感染後長達十年才出現。

paragraphs.en: Beyond the personal suffering, the resurgence of measles places a heavy burden on the healthcare system. Treating a single case of measles can cost tens of thousands of dollars, and hospitals face significant stress when dealing with these patients. Dr. Nuzzo describes the current effort to stop the virus as a game of "Whac-A-Mole," where health officials struggle to contain outbreaks as they pop up in different states. Once an outbreak is controlled in one area, it often appears in another.
paragraphs.zh: 除了個人的痛苦之外，麻疹的復燃也對醫療體系造成沉重負擔。治療單一麻疹病例的費用可能高達數萬美元，醫院在處理這些病患時面臨巨大壓力。努佐博士將目前遏止病毒的努力形容為「打地鼠」遊戲，衛生官員疲於奔命，試圖控制在不同州接連冒出的疫情。一旦某個地區的疫情受到控制，它往往又會在另一個地區出現。

paragraphs.en: Looking ahead, health experts emphasize that the measles vaccine remains one of the safest and most effective medical tools available. They urge the public to rely on scientific evidence rather than online rumors. Without a significant increase in vaccination rates, the country will likely continue to see the virus spread, putting more children and vulnerable adults at risk of serious, long-term health consequences. The goal for public health officials remains clear: to rebuild trust in vaccines and ensure that communities are protected against this dangerous and preventable disease.
paragraphs.zh: 展望未來，衛生專家強調，麻疹疫苗仍是目前最安全且有效的醫療工具之一。他們呼籲大眾應依賴科學證據，而非網路謠言。若疫苗接種率無法顯著提升，該國恐將持續面臨病毒擴散，使更多兒童與脆弱的成年人暴露在嚴重且長期的健康風險中。公共衛生官員的目標依然明確：重建對疫苗的信任，並確保社區能免受這種危險且可預防疾病的威脅。

keyTerms.definitionZh: 小群體、小區域（指在某個大範圍中，某種現象集中出現的局部地區）。
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見指衣服的口袋，這裡指特定的小群體。文中：As a result, there are now growing pockets of people who are susceptible, meaning they have no protection against the virus.

keyTerms.definitionEn: Missing parts or areas where something is lacking in a system or coverage.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 漏洞、缺失（指疫苗接種覆蓋率不足的缺口）。
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見指實體的縫隙，這裡指疫苗接種覆蓋率的不足。文中：Because it spreads so easily, even small gaps in vaccination coverage can lead to large outbreaks.

quiz.question: According to the article, what is a specific characteristic of measles that makes it particularly difficult to contain?

options.A: It can only be transmitted through direct physical contact with an infected person.
options.B: It can be spread by individuals for several days before they show any physical symptoms.
options.C: It is resistant to all known medical treatments and hospital care.
options.D: It primarily affects children who have already been vaccinated against other diseases.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第四段，麻疹患者在出現皮疹或意識到生病的前四天就已經具有傳染力，這使得病毒極難控制。選項 A 錯誤，因為麻疹是透過空氣中的微小飛沫傳播；選項 C 錯誤，文中提到疫苗是有效的醫療工具，且並未說麻疹對所有治療都有抗藥性；選項 D 錯誤，文中指出問題在於未接種疫苗的人群，而非已接種者。

quiz.question: What can be inferred about the United States' 'official elimination status' of measles?

options.A: It was lost immediately after the year 2000 due to poor public health policies.
options.B: It is currently at risk because the virus is now circulating domestically rather than just being imported.
options.C: It was never truly achieved, as occasional cases have always been present since 2000.
options.D: It is expected to be restored once the current 'Whac-A-Mole' outbreaks are fully contained.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據第二段，美國在 2000 年消滅了麻疹，當時偶發病例多為境外移入。但 Dr. Nuzzo 指出目前情況不同，病毒正在社區內人傳人，因此專家預測美國將失去消滅狀態。選項 A 與事實不符；選項 C 錯誤，因為文中明確說明 2000 年後確實達到了消滅標準；選項 D 無法從文中推論，因為目前疫苗接種率下降是結構性問題，單次控制疫情並不等於恢復地位。

quiz.question: In the sixth paragraph, what does Dr. Nuzzo mean when she describes the effort to stop the virus as a game of 'Whac-A-Mole'?

options.A: The process is simple and can be completed very quickly by health officials.
options.B: The virus is being defeated systematically in every state simultaneously.
options.C: It is a frustrating and repetitive struggle to address new outbreaks as they appear in different locations.
options.D: The government is using a new, highly effective technology to track the virus.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。Whac-A-Mole（打地鼠）是一種遊戲，地鼠剛被打下去，另一個又會從別處冒出來。文中以此比喻防疫工作：衛生官員剛控制住一個地區的疫情，病毒又在另一個州出現，顯示出防疫的無力感與不斷重複的挑戰。選項 A、B 與原意相反；選項 D 則完全偏離了這個比喻所表達的「疲於奔命」之意。

quiz.question: What is the primary message of this article regarding the current measles situation in the U.S.?

options.A: Measles is a minor illness that is being exaggerated by the media to increase hospital funding.
options.B: The U.S. healthcare system is perfectly prepared to handle any future measles outbreaks.
options.C: The resurgence of measles, driven by misinformation and low vaccination rates, poses a serious public health threat.
options.D: The only way to stop measles is to develop a completely new type of vaccine that is safer than existing ones.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。本文的核心在於探討美國麻疹病例激增的現象，指出其主因為疫苗接種率下降與網路不實資訊，並強調這對公共衛生與個人健康造成的嚴重威脅。選項 A 與文中提到的嚴重併發症事實不符；選項 B 錯誤，文中提到醫院正面臨巨大壓力；選項 D 錯誤，文中強調現有疫苗是安全有效的，重點在於提升接種率與重建信任，而非研發新疫苗。
